title: KB: Channel Implementation Decision Matrix
description:
Decision matrix from brainstorm session on implementing Telegram, WhatsApp, and Discord channel plugins.

## Context
claw-rust has a fully-built channel abstraction layer (21 adapter traits, registry, manager, delivery pipeline) but zero concrete implementations.

## SDK Choices
| Platform | SDK | Rationale |
|----------|-----|-----------|
| Telegram | teloxide-core or frankenstein | Type-safe API without competing event loop |
| WhatsApp | whatsapp-rust | Only pure Rust option, async, QR pairing |
| Discord | twilight-gateway + twilight-http | Modular, fits adapter pattern |

## Architecture Decisions
| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Crate layout | Separate crates per channel | Independent deps, compile-time selection |
| SDK integration | Thin wrappers | One lifecycle owner (ChannelManager) |
| Normalization | Convention-based (normalize.rs per crate) | Per-platform logic too different for shared trait |
| Development | All three in parallel | Trait system provides isolation |

## Options Evaluated
| Criteria | Thin Wrappers (A) | Framework Bridge (B) | Telegram-First (C) | Protocol Abstraction (D) |
|----------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|
| Architecture control | 5 | 2 | 5 | 4 |
| Development speed | 3 | 4 | 2 | 2 |
| Maintenance cost | 4 | 2 | 4 | 3 |
| Risk level | 3 | 3 | 5 | 2 |
| Future flexibility | 5 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| **Total** | **20** | **14** | **20** | **16** |

Winner: Narrative A (Thin Wrappers) — tied with C on score but preferred for parallel velocity.

## Risks Accepted
- whatsapp-rust maturity (inherited from Baileys/whatsmeow pattern)
- Pure Rust only constraint (no FFI fallback for WhatsApp)
- Parallel development of 3 channels simultaneously

Sources: teloxide (github.com/teloxide/teloxide), whatsapp-rust (github.com/jlucaso1/whatsapp-rust), twilight (twilight.rs)
close_reason: Knowledge base entry - decision matrix from brainstorm session

title: Brainstorm: Mesh Worker Architecture for claw-rust (OpenVMM-inspired)
description:
# Mesh Worker Architecture Brainstorm

## Context
Explored wrapping ALL claw-rust subsystems (channel plugins + AI agents + dispatch + gateway) in an OpenVMM-inspired mesh worker model.

## Goals (All Confirmed by User)
1. Process isolation — crash in Telegram worker doesn't take down Discord
2. Hot restart — update/reconfigure a channel without restarting the whole app
3. Uniform lifecycle protocol — every component speaks Start/Stop/Restart/Inspect
4. Scalability — workers can be distributed across processes or machines

## OpenVMM mesh_worker Key Concepts

| Concept | What It Does |
|---------|-------------|
| Worker trait | new(params) + restart(state) + run(recv: Receiver<WorkerRpc>) |
| WorkerRpc | 3 messages: Stop, Restart(state_sender), Inspect(inspector) |
| WorkerHandle | Implements Stream<Item=WorkerEvent> — Started/Stopped/Failed/RestartFailed |
| WorkerHost | Launches workers via start_worker() / launch_worker() |
| Process isolation | In-process OR separate child processes via Unix sockets/ALPC |
| Hot restart | Serialize state → new instance with restart(state) → zero-downtime |
| register_workers! macro | Distributed slice registration for auto-discovery |

## OpenVMM mesh_channel API
- Sender/MpscSender, Receiver/MpscReceiver (MPSC)
- OneshotSender/OneshotReceiver (one-time)
- Submodules: bidir, cancel, cell, deadline, error, lazy, pipe, rpc
- Cross-process: MeshPayload (protobuf serialization)

## OpenVMM mesh_process Model
- Parent spawns via Mesh::launch_host(), children join mesh
- IPC: Unix domain sockets (Linux/macOS) or ALPC (Windows)
- Invitations via env vars, each process has unique NodeId

## Current claw-rust Architecture Mapping

| Current | Mesh Equivalent |
|---------|----------------|
| ChannelManager | WorkerHost |
| ChannelPlugin impl | Worker impl (internal) |
| CancellationToken | WorkerRpc::Stop |
| run_account_loop() | Worker::run(recv) |
| AccountStatus enum | WorkerEvent stream |
| ChannelRegistry | RegisteredWorkers / register_workers! |
| Arc<RwLock<State>> | Worker-owned state (message passing) |
| tokio::spawn per account | WorkerHost::start_worker() |

### Key Existing Components
- ChannelManager (claw_channels::manager): Already does ~70% of Worker::run()
- ChannelPlugin trait: 20+ optional adapter accessors
- ChannelRegistry: Thread-safe RwLock<HashMap>
- Dispatch pipeline (claw_dispatch): typing → commands → queue → reply

## Four Narratives Evaluated

### A: Full OpenVMM Mesh Adoption
Import 10+ mesh_* crates. Full isolation, battle-tested. Very heavy dependency, overkill.

### B: Lightweight Inspired-By (RECOMMENDED)
Build claw_mesh crate (~500 lines). Worker trait + WorkerRpc + WorkerEvent + WorkerHandle. tokio::mpsc channels. Zero new deps, medium effort. Process isolation as future enhancement.

### C: Channels-Only Mesh
Only channels become workers. Low effort but hybrid bridge complexity.

### D: Actor Framework (ractor/actix/kameo)
Existing actor framework. 1 dep vs 10. Framework lock-in risk.

## User Decisions
- Scope: ALL subsystems (channels + agents + dispatch + gateway)
- All four motivations confirmed
- Direction: Leaning Narrative B (lightweight, zero deps)
- Status: PAUSED before Challenge & Refine phase

## Open Questions for Next Session
1. Should WorkerRpc include custom domain messages beyond Stop/Restart/Inspect?
2. How does the GUI observe workers? (WorkerEvent stream → egui bridge)
3. Serialization format for hot restart state? (serde JSON? bincode?)
4. How do adapter trait calls work across worker boundaries?
5. Testing strategy: in-process vs cross-process modes?
6. Migration path: incremental adoption or big-bang rewrite?

## Sources
- https://openvmm.dev/guide/
- https://openvmm.dev/rustdoc/windows/mesh_worker/index.html

title: Implement compaction engine with retry and safety
description: Port OpenClaw's compaction.ts. Build the compaction engine that summarizes old conversation turns when context window budget is exceeded. Steps: (1) Budget check - calculate total tokens of system prompt + history vs 80% of context window, (2) Turn selection - select oldest uncompacted turns, (3) Summarization - send turns to model with summarization prompt, (4) Replacement - replace original turns with summary entry, archive originals. Retry with exponential backoff on failure. Safety timeout prevents infinite retry. Fallback: truncate history if compaction repeatedly fails.
